info.title: Nightmail API
info.description: Send, receive and reply to email on your own domains. 202 means queued, not delivered.

x-quickstart.title: Add and verify your domain
x-quickstart.text: In the dashboard, open Domains and add it, or call POST /v1/domains with {"name":"acme.com"}. Publish the DNS records it returns at your DNS provider. Sending works once GET /v1/domains/{id} reports sending: "verified", usually within minutes of the records resolving. A domain whose records are still unproven after 72 hours is released.

x-quickstart.title: Create an API key
x-quickstart.text: In the dashboard, open API keys in the sidebar and choose Create key. A Send only key restricted to your domain is enough to send; it can’t read logs, so add Read permission if your code should look up outcomes. Store it as NIGHTMAIL_API_KEY on your server and never ship it to a browser.

x-quickstart.title: Send
x-quickstart.text: 202 means queued, not delivered. Follow the outcome in the dashboard’s Logs, or with GET /v1/emails/{id} and a key that has Read permission (a Send only key gets 403). Leave out region: the sender domain decides it. To test without reaching a real inbox, send to success@simulator.amazonses.com (or bounce@, complaint@, ooto@ and suppressionlist@ the same domain). Simulator sends use your daily sending limit like any other send, but never count towards your sender score.
x-quickstart.code:
curl --request POST \
  --url 'https://nightmail.com/v1/emails/send' \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer $NIGHTMAIL_API_KEY" \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --header "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  --data '{"from":"hello@acme.com","to":"you@acme.com","subject":"Hello from Nightmail","text":"It works."}'

x-quickstart.title: Receive (optional)
x-quickstart.text: Publish the receiving MX record from the domain page. Hosted Nightmail receives on a free subdomain such as reply.<your domain>, so the domain’s existing mailboxes keep working; it uses the domain itself only when its MX already points to Nightmail, or when you choose it. Create an address with POST /v1/inbound/addresses and subscribe to message.received with POST /v1/inbound/webhooks.

x-quickstart.title: Reply
x-quickstart.text: POST /v1/inbound/threads/{threadId}/reply answers the newest message from its receiving address and sets In-Reply-To and References.

bearerAuth.description: A Nightmail API key. Credentials never belong in URLs.

dashboardSession.name: nightmail.session_token
dashboardSession.description: OIDC-authenticated HttpOnly session for local development. Unsafe requests require the canonical dashboard Origin. A browser holds one session per connected account (nightmail.session_token, then nightmail.session_token.1 to .4); X-Nightmail-Account (the account ID from getCurrentIdentity) chooses the one a request acts as, otherwise the browser default. A named account without a live session gets 401 ACCOUNT_SIGNED_OUT, never another account.

secureDashboardSession.name: __Host-nightmail.session_token
secureDashboardSession.description: OIDC-authenticated Secure HttpOnly host-only session in production. Unsafe requests require the canonical dashboard Origin. A browser holds one session per connected account (__Host-nightmail.session_token, then __Host-nightmail.session_token.1 to .4); X-Nightmail-Account (the account ID from getCurrentIdentity) chooses the one a request acts as, otherwise the browser default. A named account without a live session gets 401 ACCOUNT_SIGNED_OUT, never another account.

details.description: Every problem found, when there is more than one part, such as ritual diagnostics with ritual, line, column, message and hint.

domains.description: Domains claimed in this workspace and how many can send.

inboxId.description: inbox: the agent inbox the key belongs to.

mail.description: addresses and inbox: read (mail, events, attachments), send (reply and start conversations from those addresses only), modify (mark read, archive, star, label, delete an inbox), create (create agent inboxes and use the ones it created). Empty for workspace keys.

permissions.description: Workspace permissions. Empty for a key limited to addresses or an inbox: see access.

expiresAt.description: When a key limited to an expiring inbox stops working (the inbox's deletion time). Null otherwise.

permissions.description: Workspace keys: read, send and manage. Defaults to send.

domains.description: Workspace keys: sender domains it is limited to, including their subdomains. Defaults to all.

inboxId.description: An active agent inbox. The key stops working when the inbox is deleted, and when an expiring inbox ends.

CreateApiKeyAccess.description: What the key is limited to. Defaults to the workspace. A key for addresses or an inbox takes its permissions in access.mail and can never send from other addresses, read other mail or manage the workspace.

counts.description: Active members only. Suppressed takes precedence over consent; subscribed, unsubscribed, unknown and suppressed are mutually exclusive and sum to total.

evidence.description: How these people agreed to marketing email, for example "Opted in at checkout". Stored with each consent record.

consent.description: Records that everyone in this import agreed to receive marketing email. It changes only contacts with no consent decision yet: prior opt-outs stay unsubscribed and suppressed addresses stay suppressed. Omit it to import without consent.

html.description: Concrete Nightmail block HTML shared with the visual editor and renderer. Email-safe inline styles support color, typography, spacing, borders, radius and dimensions. Templates do not accept {{placeholders}}; edit the copied campaign when personalization is needed. Call getContentGuide before writing.

headers.description: Extra MIME headers, 8 KB total. The 15-header limit includes generated headers (two for marketing and any mailbox threading headers). In-Reply-To and References must be <id@domain> Message-IDs and thread the message in the recipient's mail client.

priority.description: Send order: contacts whose property equals an earlier value are reviewed and released first; everyone else follows. Useful with paced sending, e.g. { property: "plan", values: ["active", "former"] }.

CampaignDraft.description: Drafts may omit sender, subject, content and audience until review or send, except that domain-restricted keys must supply a From address on one of their domains. Content is block HTML (see html); the same form is what the dashboard composer reads and writes, so people and agents edit one document. Simple {{name}} personalization works in text and quoted href/alt attributes; values are HTML-escaped and rendered URLs are validated. Durable campaign preparation is bounded and runs in background jobs.

source.description: Domain publishing the effective TXT record; may be the organizational domain.

dmarc.description: Last DNS and SES observation for this From domain. Null when unchecked, unavailable or stale. Alignment describes configured identifiers, not a delivery verdict.

releasesAt.description: Hosted only: when this domain is released if its records are still unproven (72 hours after it was added). Null once ownership has been proven.

code.description: cname: the host is a CNAME, so it cannot have an MX (RFC 1034). foreign_mx: another provider receives its mail. split: other MX records share its mail. wildcard: a *.domain CNAME or MX answers for it. bane_record: it is one of Nightmail’s own names (custom MAIL FROM, ownership TXT, DKIM). host_taken: another claim, possibly in another workspace, receives on it. claimed: another workspace claimed it, or a name between it and this domain, in any scope. delegated: it is a delegated zone with its own NS records. claimed and delegated hosts never receive here. mx_missing: its MX disappeared after setup. wrong_region and null_mx: its MX points elsewhere in SES or refuses mail. proof_stale / identity_stale: the ownership TXT proof or the SES verification is out of date.

blocking.description: True when receiving there cannot work until DNS or the choice changes.

suggestion.description: A free subdomain to use instead.

receivingIssue.description: Hosted only: receiving needs attention. Set by the DNS checks that run when a receiving host is suggested or chosen, on Check now and in the hourly recheck. Null when the receiving record is clear.

region.description: Regional BYO defaults to the first enabled region, otherwise Ohio.

url.description: Write-only HTTPS endpoint. Only the last four characters are shown; omit url on update to keep the saved URL.

headers.description: Configured names only for readers. Managers also see a masked hint and the time the header list was last replaced.

secret.description: The signing secret, whsec_ followed by 32 base64 bytes. Read it again with revealWebhookSecret.

headers.description: Write-only custom HTTP request headers, e.g. Authorization. Up to 10 unique names (case-insensitive) and 8192 UTF-8 bytes of names and values. Omit on update to keep, supply the complete list to replace, or [] to clear. Transport, Cookie and Nightmail delivery headers are reserved.

suppressionReason.description: Reason recorded when this send was suppressed. For a multi-recipient send blocked locally, this is the first blocked recipient in To, Cc, Bcc order.

state.description: warmup while calibrating: until 100 real recipients were accepted and 24 hours passed (Hosted), or the first 100 emails (self-hosted).

firstEmails.description: Real recipients accepted, counted up to 100.

needed.description: Accepted recipients before the first score (100).

calibratedAt.description: When the 100th recipient was accepted; the score starts 24 hours later.

score.description: 0–100, one decimal; null while warming up. It moves towards target by at most +5 or −10 a day.

target.description: Where the score is heading: quality shrunk towards 60 by the decayed volume (250 emails count as much as the prior).

raw.description: Quality: the weighted factor result before shrinkage. It is the ceiling the score can reach.

next.description: The next grade up and the score it starts at.

history.description: The published daily score, oldest first, up to 14 days.

key.description: complaints, content (the spam screen), bounces (to known recipients), hygiene (list quality: first sends and suppression hits), auth, engagement.

weight.description: Share of the score, out of 100, when every factor is measured.

value.description: The measured rate or ratio, decayed with a 30-day half-life; null when neutral.

score.description: 0–100 for this factor; null when neutral.

source.description: Neutral factors are left out and the measured ones re-weighted.

daily.description: Recipients per rolling 24 hours that admission enforces now. Null when the workspace has no hosted limit.

band.description: The limit the score earns, before a resume or strike reduction.

next.description: The next band up and the score it starts at.

restore.description: After a resume: the limit is at most this many recipients a day until then (half the limit before the resume, unless an operator restored all of it).

SenderLimit.description: Hosted only: the daily limit the score sets and what changes it.

step.description: ok; notice (dashboard only); warn (limit frozen, owners emailed); restrict (marketing held, transactional flows); pause (all sending stopped).

pauseKind.description: bounce: only transactional bounces paused it, and an owner may resume it once in 30 days. full: complaints, the spam screen, abuse or an AWS tenant pause; an operator reviews it.

marketingRelease.description: An owner released a restrict: marketing is at this share of its allowance until then.

strikes.description: Pauses in the last 90 days. A second caps the limit at 50% for 7 days after the resume; a third needs an operator for any resume.

selfService.description: Whether an owner or admin can release this step from the dashboard (POST /v1/sender-score/release), and if not, why.

version.description: Changes with every change of standing; account.standing.changed carries it.

bouncedRemoved.description: Contacts that bounced or complained are removed.

listSourceConfirmed.description: Every contact opted in; no bought or old lists.

Dashboard sessions may receive a cached result until the workspace creates an email or records an email event, or for up to 60 seconds, and compute at most 30 such Overview reads a minute: past that they get their last result (cache header stale) or 429 DASHBOARD_RATE_LIMITED. Outcomes use current email state and all recorded events, including events after to; this is not a historical state snapshot. Each outcome counts distinct emails, so replays do not inflate counts and outcomes may overlap. Accepted (bucket sent) means evidence of provider acceptance, not merely queued/created. Daily UTC creation buckets contain count=created emails. Granularity defaults to day; granularity=hour additionally returns hourly UTC creation buckets with canonical ISO dates such as 2026-09-12T01:00:00.000Z, while preserving daily buckets and totals. Absent buckets mean zero created emails and zero outcomes; no moving averages are applied. Engagement is observed, not verified human activity.

post.summary: Create an agent inbox
post.description: Creates an inbox with a fresh address. Set type=persistent for forever retention (no lease or default per-inbox cap; workspace manage permission). The default is an expiring inbox on one of the workspace’s active receiving domains, or a sandbox inbox that needs no DNS. Then wait for mail with GET /v1/inboxes/{id}/messages?wait=30 (or the SDK’s waitForMessage). Needs a workspace admin or an inbound key with create permission. Limits: 60 creates per minute and 1,000 retained inboxes (including grace and pending erasure) per workspace. Errors: RECEIVING_DOMAIN_REQUIRED and RECEIVING_NOT_ACTIVE name the DNS step to take; ADDRESS_TAKEN, ADDRESS_RETIRED, EPHEMERAL_INBOX_LIMIT, INBOX_CREATE_RATE (with Retry-After) and IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT.

type.description: persistent: a real address kept until explicitly deleted. ephemeral: a real address on one of your active receiving domains. sandbox: an address on a .invalid host that receives nothing from the internet; fill it with POST /v1/inboxes/{id}/simulate.

ttlSeconds.description: Lifetime before the inbox expires: 60 seconds to 30 days. Default 24 hours.

graceHours.description: Hours after expiry during which new mail is still stored but held, before everything is erased. 0–168, default 24.

domain.description: Receiving host for the address, such as reply.acme.com. Default: the workspace’s oldest active receiving host.

localPart.description: Admin REST only; provisioning keys and MCP must omit this. Default: 10 random characters, which nobody can guess.

name.description: A label for the dashboard and lists. Replies use it as the From display name.

metadata.description: Your own JSON, up to 16 KiB. Returned as is.

clientId.description: Idempotency key. Repeating a create with the same clientId and body returns the same inbox (200, without the key secret); a different body is a 409.

messages.description: Messages delivered before new mail is held. At most 200.

bytes.description: Stored bytes before new mail is held. At most 25 MiB.

limits.description: Optional delivery caps. Temporary inboxes default to 200 messages and 25 MiB; persistent inboxes have no default delivery cap. Held mail is stored and readable, never dropped.

send.description: Replies only go to people who wrote to this inbox. Sandbox inboxes never send.

permissions.description: read: list and read mail. modify: mark read, simulate, delete the inbox. send: reply (needs send.enabled).

credential.description: Also create a key that can use only this inbox. Its secret is returned once and it expires with the inbox. Use it as a bearer token for this API or hosted MCP.
